justiceSays.line: Wanjiru spends the afternoon with the tree with orange fruit, soft when ripe — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. Edible, but it argues on the way down. The fire's verdict: food, carefully. Small amounts.
Word reaches you, days late: Nolan stands accused over what happened to Mason. There's going to be a moot. People are choosing sides.

Carlos leans in, voice low. "Here's what we figured out about Lockpick. Buy it off. It steals FIRST and fights second — but it CANNOT resist food. OFFER FOOD in the fight: it drops your things mid-scamper for the meal. A bribe is cheaper than a chase."

Theo has been talking at the fires. Enough voices — tonight they call a moot. Nolan answers for what happened to Mason.
Theo calls the moot. The fire gets built up — word travels fast, and almost everyone comes.
The fire is built high. Nobody speaks while the count is taken — you can hear the wind past the edge of the light.
Esmeralda counts on their fingers, twice, like they don't trust the first number. Then, to the fire: "1 for guilty. 5 against."
A long exhale moves around the fire like weather. "Not guilty — this time."

The moot turns to you. Your vote matters here — and everyone will remember it.
The moot doesn't wait forever. Two days of silence from the fire's edge — the count is taken without you.

Esmeralda counts on their fingers, twice, like they don't trust the first number. Then, to the fire: "0 for guilty. 7 against."
A long exhale moves around the fire like weather. "Not guilty — this time."
They're named, every one: Tomás Larsen, Peter Weiss, Victor Nair. Your move — ask them questions (up to three), call a MOOT on it, or turn them away at the edge of the firelight.
They waited three days at the edge of your fire. Nobody called the moot. Tomás nods — not angry, just done — and they walk.

💡 COUNTER LEARNED — Gavel: Confess first — take the lighter verdict. It accuses, waits a full round, then the verdict falls. Confess first — out loud, where everyone can hear — and the verdict falls lighter. But witnesses remember the confession; it is on the record. (You lived to tell it, twice — and now you see the pattern.)
